div.head: Ps Cn for 29
div.ab: Si quis uero ilicem, aut arborem aliquam que uictum feris suppeditat, sciderit, preter fractionem regalis chacee emendet regi uiginti solidos.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 625 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: But if anyone cuts down an oak, or any tree that supplies food to the beasts, besides [the penalty for] breach of the royal chase let him pay the king twenty shillings compensation.

note.seg: das Fällen fruchttragender Bäume bestrafen auch andere Germanen strenger; Wilda Strafrecht 934. Sogar wo der Grundeigenthümer anderes Holz im Königsforst fällen darf, bleibt die Eiche geschützt; Turner Sel. pleas p. lxxiij. Die reguarda forestae seit Heinrich II. notiren unumquemque ceppum de quercu uel fago; Rog. Hov. II 243, wiederholt a. 1229 ed. Shirley Royal letters I 347

Other Germanic peoples too punish the felling of fruit-bearing trees more severely; Wilda, Strafrecht 934. Even where the landowner may fell other wood in the royal forest, the oak remains protected; Turner, Sel. pleas p. lxxiij. The reguarda forestae from Henry II on record unumquemque ceppum de quercu uel fago; Rog. Hov. II 243, repeated a. 1229, ed. Shirley, Royal letters I 347
